finalText:
## What happened

**One-line version:** Redis died, the app fell back to reading the datastore directly, that overloaded the store, request queues grew unbounded for 17 minutes until worker-2 OOM'd and the supervisor killed the API.

### Timeline (all `2026-07-04`)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00 – 02:14:03 | Healthy. `/users`, `/orders`, `/health` all 200. Cache hit ratio 0.90–0.98 the whole time. |
| **02:14:07.113** | `ERROR [api] redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379` ← **root cause** (`app.log:182`) |
| 02:14:07.114 | `WARN [api] cache layer degraded — falling back to direct store reads` (`:183`) |
| 02:14:08 | Cache miss storm begins, keys `orders:1000`–`orders:1199` |
| 02:14:10 | First `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` |
| 02:14:12 | Queue depth 52 — starts climbing ~30/min, linearly, never recovers |
| 02:15:26 → 02:31:26 | 13 Redis reconnect attempts, **all** ECONNREFUSED |
| 02:29:12 | Queue depth **502**, crosses the stated `max 500` — and keeps going (`:647`) |
| 02:31:24 | Queue depth 568 |
| 02:31:44 | `ERROR [worker-2] JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)` (`:717`) |
| 02:31:45 | `FATAL [supervisor] worker-2 exited with code 134, restarting` |
| **02:31:52** | `FATAL [supervisor] api unresponsive, killing process group — service down` |

Volume: 188 ERROR / 348 WARN, of which 173 are the timeout and 13 the Redis reconnect. Everything after 02:14:07 is downstream noise from that one event.

### The four things that actually made this bad

1. **No circuit breaker on the cache fallback.** Losing Redis shouldn't be fatal, but "fall back to direct store reads" sent the full uncached read volume at the datastore. Every 5s timeout after 02:14:10 is the store buckling. The cache outage became a store outage became an app outage.

2. **The queue limit isn't enforced.** Depth is logged as `(max 500)` but sails straight through 500 to 568 with no shedding, no 503s, no backpressure. That backlog is literally what the OOM message blames — `JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)`. If 500 had been a real ceiling, worker-2 survives.

3. **Reconnect has no backoff and no ceiling.** The 13 attempts are exactly 80s apart — flat interval, not exponential. 17 minutes of identical ECONNREFUSED with nothing escalating. Nothing in the log suggests anyone or anything gave up, alerted, or tried a replica.

4. **The hot keyset is tiny.** The miss storm cycles through only `orders:1000`–`orders:1199` — about 200 keys, repeating. A small in-process LRU would have absorbed nearly all of this and made the Redis loss a non-event.

### Two caveats

- **These logs are from July 4th, not last night.** The file starts `2026-07-04T02:00` and ends `2026-07-04T02:31:52`. If prod fell over on Aug 31 / Sep 1, this is a stale or unrotated file and you're looking at the wrong incident — worth checking your rotation before you act on any of the above. (If the July 4th incident is what you meant, disregard.)
- **The log ends at the kill, so there's no recovery data.** No restart-success line, no Redis coming back. Whatever brought it back isn't in this file, and neither is confirmation that `worker-1` or `scheduler` ever died — only worker-2 and api have fatals.

I'd start by checking why `10.0.0.12:6379` refused connections at 02:14:07 — ECONNREFUSED means nothing was listening, so that's a Redis crash/restart/eviction, not a network partition. There's no `src/` in this directory, only `package.json` (`ioredis ^5.4.1`), so I couldn't check the actual fallback and queue code — point me at the repo and I can look at where the limit is supposed to be enforced.
